elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Section 7.3 as rendered warrants only substantial conformance of the Software and MarketSite.net Service to the Documentation and defect-free media; no professional/workmanlike standard of performance appears anywhere in the rendered language, and the redline did not add one.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: "Commerce One warrants that the Software and MarketSite.net Service will perform in substantial accordance with the Documentation"; "Software" and "Documentation" are both defined terms.

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Rendered period is "ninety (90) days from the Effective Date (the \"Warranty Period\")" — well short of 12 months; the drafter expressly declined to seek the preferred period.
The single Warranty Period of ninety (90) days covers the MarketSite.net Service as well as the Software.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "Commerce One shall take all commercially reasonable efforts to correct the Software and MarketSite.net Service, or if correction ... is reasonably not possible, replace such Software and MarketSite.net Service free of charge."
"In the event any such breach of warranty can not be reasonably corrected at Commerce One's sole expense, Corio has the right to terminate this Agreement and receive a refund of all prepaid fees."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty appears in the rendered Section 7.3/7.4 language; none was added.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: "Commerce One warrants that during the Warranty Period the Software and MarketSite.net Service is free of any willfully introduced computer virus, or any other similar harmful, malicious or hidden program or data..." (limited to the Warranty Period, but the no-malicious-code warranty is expressly present).

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Rendered: "the Software and MarketSite.net Service will perform in substantial accordance with the Documentation ... for a period of ninety (90) days from the Effective Date (the \"Warranty Period\")". The December 31, 1999 outside date that would have truncated the 90 days (90 days from the 29 October 1999 Effective Date runs to late January 2000) has been deleted, so the full 90 days survives.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: The MarketSite.net Service is covered by the same conformance warranty and the same ninety (90) day Warranty Period, exceeding the 30-day floor.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Retained: commercially reasonable efforts to correct, and free-of-charge replacement where correction is not reasonably possible; defective media also replaced.
Retained: termination plus "a refund of all prepaid fees" where the breach cannot reasonably be corrected — a refund remedy is available on breach of the conformance warranty.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete on the operative rendered text: 90-day Software-to-Documentation warranty, the same 90-day period for the MarketSite.net Service (above the 30-day floor), correction/free replacement, and a refund of all prepaid fees.

Preferred level is not reached: no professional-and-workmanlike services standard, no compliance-with-laws warranty, and the software period is 90 days rather than 12 months. These are noted, not required, because the fallback is complete.

Minimality holds. Only two edits were made inside the target element: sixty (60) → ninety (90), and deletion of "but in no event not later than December 31, 1999". The outside date deletion is necessary rather than cosmetic — with an Effective Date of 29 October 1999, a 31 December 1999 cap would have cut the period to roughly 63 days and contradicted the extension. No survival tail, expense language, extra remedies or boilerplate were added.

Intent is preserved. The defined term "Warranty Period" is retained and still anchors the malicious-code warranty, the media-replacement sentence, the correction/refund cascade, the sole-and-exclusive-remedies sentence and the exclusions list; no cross-reference is left dangling and no retained sentence now contradicts the 90-day period.

The underlying finding of deviation is correct: at 60 days (further truncated by the 31 December 1999 cap) the original Software conformance warranty fell below the 90-day fallback floor, which is a material term rather than a minor sub-element.
